intro: Daniel Fox is a fractional B2C CMO and marketing leader for established, profitable consumer businesses (typically $3M-$12M revenue) selling a considered, high-ticket purchase. The work is to run the whole marketing function - strategy through pipeline - and answer for the number, rather than hand a business another vendor doing activity without leadership. He founded, built, and sold Skreened, a custom-apparel company, and has run dozens of fractional engagements since.

pages.title: Fractional CMO for Your Next Stage of Growth
pages.desc: Fractional CMO and marketing leadership for established, profitable companies. I run the whole marketing function, strategy through pipeline. Marketing for your next stage of growth.

pages.title: What Does a Fractional CMO Do? The Whole Function
pages.desc: What a fractional CMO does: runs the entire marketing function (strategy, content, SEO, AI-search visibility, paid, capture, nurture, creative, and measurement) part-time, with one number to hold.

pages.title: Is a Fractional CMO Right for Your Business?
pages.desc: When a fractional CMO is the right call for a considered, high-ticket business, and when it isn't. A plain fit check.

pages.title: Fractional B2C CMO: Marketing Leadership for Consumer Businesses
pages.desc: What a fractional B2C CMO is: executive marketing leadership for consumer businesses selling considered, high-ticket purchases, built around one question: why consumers buy. What the seat covers and who it fits.

pages.title: About Daniel Fox: Fractional CMO & Operator
pages.desc: I'm Daniel Fox, a fractional CMO who has personally run the marketing function for dozens of high-ticket businesses, and who built and sold a company of my own.

pages.title: Start a Conversation with a Fractional CMO
pages.desc: Tell me about your business in two minutes. A short conversation tells us both whether the math and the fit are there. No pitch deck, no pressure.

pages.title: Demand Generation for High-Ticket Buyers
pages.desc: How to generate steady demand for a considered, high-ticket purchase, and why one accountable leader running the whole marketing function beats paying for scattered activity that never compounds.

pages.title: Fractional CMO vs. Agency: Which Do You Need?
pages.desc: Agency, freelancer, or fractional marketing leader? A plain breakdown for owners of high-ticket businesses on who actually answers for the outcome, and who just runs tasks.

pages.title: SEO for High-Ticket Businesses
pages.desc: How a high-ticket business wins search for a researched, considered purchase, and why content and SEO only compound when one leader runs the plan. A fractional CMO's view.

pages.title: Getting Found in AI Search Results
pages.desc: When buyers ask an assistant to recommend a business like yours, will it name you? A clear look at earning visibility in AI answers without chasing vanity metrics.

pages.title: How to Generate Leads Beyond Referrals
pages.desc: Real lead generation for high-ticket businesses (beyond referrals and luck), and why a fenced channel you can measure is the one that scales. A fractional CMO's view.

pages.title: Fractional CMO Insights: Demand for High-Ticket Businesses
pages.desc: How demand actually works for considered, high-ticket purchases: the fractional-CMO category argument, plus plain answers to the questions high-ticket business owners ask next.

pages.title: How Much Does a Fractional CMO Cost?
pages.desc: What a fractional CMO costs: most run $8,000 to $22,000 a month; mine start at $10,000. Why the rate is the wrong first question, and how to weigh it against a full-time hire and the agency spend you already carry. Daniel Fox, fractional CMO.

pages.title: Do I Need a Fractional CMO or an Agency?
pages.desc: Agencies execute inside your current answers about the customer. A fractional CMO reopens those answers. If your answers are producing your ceiling, execution isn't the constraint. Daniel Fox.

pages.title: Marketing Coordinator vs. Strategist: Which Do You Need?
pages.desc: Your marketing person left and you are choosing a replacement. A coordinator executes a strategy; a strategist decides what it is. How to tell which role your business actually needs. Daniel Fox, fractional CMO.

pages.title: Why Is My ROAS Declining When Nothing Changed?
pages.desc: Return on ad spend slipping with steady spend and unchanged campaigns usually means your perfect-fit cohort is saturating. Why the dashboard can't tell saturation from noise, and what to do.

pages.title: How Do I Know If My Market Is Saturated?
pages.desc: A saturating market and a market you address wrong produce the same silence. The wrong market won't tell you they're the wrong market. How to separate the two. Daniel Fox, fractional CMO.

pages.title: Why Aren't My Ads Converting With a New Audience?
pages.desc: The messaging that built trust with your first audience is actively disqualifying the next one. Trust-builders become door-closers. What to do instead. Daniel Fox, fractional CMO.

pages.title: Should I Rebrand or Reposition?
pages.desc: Most rebrands are an expensive way to avoid a sentence-level fix. The adjacent market usually needs a reframe, not a new identity. Run the cheap experiment first. Daniel Fox, fractional CMO.

pages.title: Product-Market Fit Has a Ceiling
pages.desc: The fit that got you to your first few million covers one segment, one channel, one story. Why product-market fit is a gradient you keep climbing, and how the next fit hides in plain sight.

pages.title: The Small Tweak That Opens the Next Market
pages.desc: When growth stalls, founders reach for a rebrand. Usually the next market needs a reframe, not a new story. How to change one variable and reach the adjacent cohort.

pages.title: Your Answers About the Customer Are Working as Designed
pages.desc: Your answer to 'who is our customer' is calibrated to produce exactly your current numbers. Why the question gets filed as settled, and how to reopen it deliberately.

pages.title: Your Dashboard Can't Tell You What's Wrong
pages.desc: Declining return on ad spend has three different causes and one identical-looking graph. Why analytics flag the symptom, and where the real diagnosis actually happens.

pages.title: What I Believe About Why Growth Stalls
pages.desc: Seven positions on why a profitable company hits a marketing ceiling, and why the answer that built your revenue is the one keeping it where it is. Daniel Fox, fractional CMO.

pages.title: Projective Empathy: Reading Your Marketing From the Buyer's Seat
pages.desc: Projective empathy is the trained practice of inhabiting a buyer's value structure and reading your own marketing from inside it. A method by Daniel Fox, fractional CMO, drawing on Spiral Dynamics.
